oracle: byte-based SourceSpan line/column convention: 1-based, newline resets column, UTF-8 columns count bytes
scope: The existing global byte-offset mapping regression remains covered. The new line_col_span_global callable maps ordered endpoints in one bounded prefix walk for canonical positive-stride pages, with fast paths for byte-zero and identical endpoints. Reference interpreter, Cranelift, and a fresh canonical VM artifact agree with the byte-based SourceSpan convention across 23 page-layout inputs and 25 span requests covering newline edges, UTF-8 byte columns, clamped offsets, empty input, and a 64 KiB source. Within the tested span pairs, canonical VM transition counts fell 7.91% versus two separate lookups at the same endpoints. This does not prove full Source module behavior, Language verified-fact reuse, Unicode-scalar columns, or compiler succession.

canonical_vm_wall_seconds.comparison_note: Single-run VM batch observations on the same 85 requests; they show the measured workload result, not a general speed guarantee.

reference_and_cranelift_child_cpu_second.comparison_note: Harness child CPU includes process and compilation work; the committed verification run reused frontend/backend caches, so no CPU percent change is claimed.

canonical_vm_peak_rss_kib.comparison_note: Process peak RSS; cgroup memory counters were unavailable.

baseline_comparison.interpretation: The prefix scan reduced aggregate reference-interpreter steps by 19.64% and canonical-VM steps by 19.57% across the same 85 requests. Both candidate VM timing samples were 9.23–9.32 seconds versus the baseline sample at 11.38 seconds. Maximum single-call steps remained effectively unchanged because end-of-source offsets scan the full input; CPU comparison includes compilation cache-state differences and is not claimed as a speedup.
